decision.observation: 9 mph, gear 1, timer 01:32.082, red X lit, all dots dark. The car has drifted onto the grass at the left verge and is no longer on the gravel; the track edge and its marker posts are a couple of metres to its right, and the road curves right ahead with pines close on the left.
decision.hypothesis: Straight throttle keeps the car drifting left off the track, and pine trunks are close on that side. The car must be brought back right, so a very short right steer (0.2 s instead of 0.3 s) is worth trying even though longer right steers zeroed the speed - staying on grass risks a pin.
decision.memory: Speed fell 11 -> 9 while drifting off the left edge: leaving the track costs speed even with throttle. Note whether a 0.2 s steer is less destructive than 0.3 s.
